ByteSize.description: A byte size: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `b`, `kb`, `mb`, `gb`, or `tb`; units are binary, so `1kb` is 1024 bytes.

ChangedPaths.description: Whether the changed project paths ride the hook's command line.

oneOf.description: The command runs exactly as configured.

The changed project paths follow the configured `arguments`, in byte
order, for a tool that takes files.

CommandHook.description:
One `[[hooks]]` command the server runs inside the changed tree.
Every key is required; the schema carries no defaults.

arguments.description: The program's literal arguments, in order. May be empty.

changed_paths.description: Whether the server appends changed project paths after `arguments`, in byte order.

determinism.description: Whether an identical tree and environment are expected to reproduce the result.

environment.description: Environment values added to the environment the server inherited.

failure_severity.description: Severity the server reports when the hook does not pass.

guarantees.description: What a passing validation establishes. Transform hooks cannot declare guarantees.

id.description: Label for this hook's results, unique within the list.

kind.description: What the hook is: a formatter, test suite, linter, build, or another command.

output_limit.description: Bytes of each output stream the server keeps, 256b to 4kb. The full size is still reported.

program.description:
The executable the server starts. A bare name resolves through `PATH`; a path resolves
below `working_directory`. Absolute paths and `.` or `..` segments are refused.

timeout.description: Wall-clock bound before the server kills the process, 1ms to 1h.

type.description: How the server runs the hook; `command` is the only type.

working_directory.description:
Directory the process starts in, relative to the changed tree's root. Empty selects the
root. Absolute paths and `.` or `..` segments are refused.

writes.description: Source files the server permits the hook to change.

oneOf.description: Only what this request touched.
Every visible file of the workspace.
The workspace's resolved dependencies.
The workspace, its dependencies, and the standard library together.

CoverageScope.description:
What a completeness statement covers - everything the request asked for, one file, or a
standing scope the answer holds over.

oneOf.description: A standing scope identified by its name.
A single unit is just a file: the claim holds for that path and says nothing about any other.

unit.description: The file the claim is about.

Determinism.description:
Whether an identical tree and environment are expected to reproduce a
hook's result.

oneOf.description: The same tree and environment give the same answer.
The result may vary between identical runs.

Duration.description: A duration: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`.

EngineConfiguration.description:
One `[engines.<name>]` table: an external LSP server Rift may start.

The key is the engine's name, a lowercase word in the language-name
charset. Rift starts the engine on the first request for a language it
serves, speaks LSP to it over stdio, and reuses the running engine
across requests. The engine never writes: it proposes edits, and Rift
applies them through its own change path.

arguments.description: The program's literal arguments, in order. May be empty.

environment.description:
Environment values added on top of the environment the server
inherited.

initialization_options.description:
Options handed to the engine at initialize. Must be a JSON object
when present; the engine defines its meaning.

languages.description:
The languages this engine serves: a language name, or `name:dialect`
to pin a dialect. Each segment belongs to at most one engine across
the whole `[engines]` table. A segment no syntax provider knows is
accepted: an engine may serve languages the syntax tier does not.

output_limit.description:
Bytes of the engine's standard error Rift keeps, 1kb to 8mb. The
full size is still reported.

program.description:
The executable Rift starts inside the workspace root. An absolute
path is refused; the name resolves through `PATH`.

request_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on each later engine request, 1s to 10m.

restart.description:
How often Rift replaces this engine on its own, and over what
window; the budget spent, the engine's own failure surfaces.

retry.description:
How often Rift sends this engine the same request again while its
answer stays unsettled - a refusal the engine invites again, or an
answer it gave while still analyzing - and how the waits between
those attempts grow.

startup_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on the engine's initialize handshake, 1s to 10m.

ExecutionConfiguration.description:
The `[execution]` table. `execute` stays off until `allow` names the
languages caller-provided code may run as.

allow.description:
Language selectors enabled for `execute`: a language name, or
`name:dialect` to pin a dialect. Empty keeps execution off.

max_code.description: Bytes one submitted block may hold, 1b to 32kb.

max_concurrent.description: Evaluations running at once across the whole workspace.

max_output.description: Bytes each captured stream keeps, up to 16kb.

FileId.description:
Identity of one file in the tree a request targets. The path after `rift://file/` is a
`ProjectPath` in canonical percent-encoding. The server re-validates the decoded path
wherever a `FileId` arrives, so the `ProjectPath` exclusions hold for every consumer,
whatever schema its implementation generated from.

GuaranteeKind.description: A property a verifier can establish about an applied change.

oneOf.description: The changed source parses.
Names still resolve to what they resolved to before the change.
References to the changed declarations were updated with them.
The change's behavior was exercised, such as by a test suite.

HistoryConfiguration.description:
The `[providers.history]` table. The history provider's cost scales with
how far back it walks, so its depth is the budget worth setting.

enabled.description: Whether the history provider runs at all.

max_revisions.description: Revisions the walk covers from the current head, newest first.

HookFailureSeverity.description: Severity the server reports when a hook does not pass.

oneOf.description: The hook result reports a warning.
The hook result reports an error.

HookGuarantee.description: What a passing run of one hook establishes about the change it checked.

detail.description: The exact property the hook checks, and the limits on reading a pass.

HookKind.description: What a hook is, as workspace configuration presents it.

oneOf.description: A source formatter.
A test suite.
A linter.
A build.
A hook none of the other kinds describe.

HookType.description:
How a hook runs; `command` - an executable started directly, without a
shell - is the only type.

oneOf.description: An executable Rift starts directly inside the changed tree.

HookWrites.description: Source writes the server may retain from one hook.

oneOf.description: A validation hook that may not change source files.
A transform hook that may change only paths changed before hooks ran.
A transform hook that may change any source file in the workspace.

LexicalSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.lexical]` table: what the lexical ranking contributes to a
fused score.

weight.description:
The lexical ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0. It and
`[search.semantic].weight` must sum to 1: a fused score is the weighted
average of the two rankings, and a pair summing to anything else scales
every score rather than trading one ranking against the other.

LogsConfiguration.description:
The `[logs]` table. The server records its own diagnostics in the workspace
database, where `rift://logs` reads them back, and this table bounds how
many records the store keeps, how many one read returns, and which targets
are captured at all. The server reads the table at startup, so a change
applies on the next start.

capture.description:
Which targets are recorded, in the `RUST_LOG` spelling `tracing` takes:
comma-separated `target=level` pairs. A target this filter excludes
never reaches the store, whatever the stderr diagnostics carry.

page_records.description: Records one `rift://logs` read returns at most, 1 to 5000.

retention_records.description: Records the store keeps before the oldest are dropped, 100 to 1000000.

PathPattern.description:
Project-relative glob using *, ?, **, and character classes. Forward-slash separated on
every platform, whatever separator the host OS uses natively.

PortRange.description:
The `server.port_range` table: the inclusive loopback range the server
picks the first free port from.

max.description: The highest port the server may bind, at or above `min`.

min.description: The lowest port the server may bind, 1024 or above.

ProjectPath.description:
One path below the workspace root, using forward slashes and UTF-8 in Unicode NFC - Rift
normalizes what it emits and what it accepts, and compares byte-for-byte. The empty path
names the root itself. Absolute paths, backslashes, control characters, empty segments,
and `.` or `..` segments are refused before the filesystem is touched. The limit is 1000
UTF-8 bytes, not characters. A workspace holding two entries whose NFC forms are equal
fails the read that touches them with `content_unavailable`.

ProvidersConfiguration.description:
The `[providers]` table: the built-in providers run without
configuration, and this table bounds or disables them.

RestartPolicy.description:
How often Rift may replace one language engine on its own, and over
what window.

A restart is any start after the first: the first is the start, and
every start that follows it replaces an engine that ended, failed to
start, or stopped answering. A restart older than `window` no longer
counts, so a workspace whose engine dies once a day keeps its full
budget while a crash-looping one spends it and stops.

attempts.description: Restarts allowed inside one window, 0 to 16. Zero never restarts.

window.description: Span the restarts are counted over, 1s to 1d.

RetryPolicy.description:
How often one unsettled operation is attempted again, and how the
waits between attempts grow.

Attempts are numbered from one and the first is counted, so
`attempts = 1` never resends. Each wait is twice the one before it,
held at `delay_limit`; a `delay_limit` below `delay` therefore holds
every wait at `delay_limit`.

The waits carry no jitter. Jitter spreads a set of independent retriers
apart so they stop arriving together; requests to one language engine
serialize on that engine's own slot, so there is never such a set, and
the sequence stays a function of the attempt number alone.

attempts.description: Attempts one operation takes, the first counted, 1 to 64.

delay.description:
Wait before the second attempt, 1ms to 1m. Every later wait
doubles the one before it.

delay_limit.description: Longest wait between two attempts, 1ms to 10m.

SearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search]` table. Search fuses a lexical ranking with a semantic one:
`lexical` and `semantic` weigh the two against each other, `fusion_k` sets
how sharply a top rank counts, `pool_slots` and `busy_timeout` bound the
shared `SQLite` connections behind search and logs, and `text` bounds
lexical chunks derived from visible text files.

busy_timeout.description:
Wall-clock budget one connection waits for a database lock held by
another process before `SQLITE_BUSY`, 100ms to 30s.

fusion_k.description:
The reciprocal-rank fusion constant, 1 to 1000. A result scores as the
weighted sum of `1 / (k + rank)` over the rankings that returned it, so
a larger value flattens the contribution curve and lets agreement
between the two rankings outweigh one ranking's top position.

lexical.description: The lexical ranking's share of a fused score.

pool_slots.description:
Pooled `SQLite` connections the workspace database may open at once,
1 to 16. Search reads and stored logs share this pool.

semantic.description:
The embedding model that adds semantic ranking, and the bounds its
preparation runs under.

text.description: Chunking policy for visible text files in lexical search.

SemanticSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.semantic]` table: the embedding model that ranks a query
against code sharing no word with it, and the bounds its preparation runs
under.

Preparation runs behind the answers. A search issued before the vectors are
in is answered lexically and carries a warning naming what is still
missing.

batch_declarations.description:
Declarations one embedding pass hands the encoder at once, 1 to 256.
Attention memory grows with the square of `max_tokens`, so a raised
token window wants a lowered batch.

candidates.description:
Declarations the semantic ranking returns before the two rankings are
fused, 1 to 1000.

candidates_per_file.description:
Declarations one file may contribute to the semantic ranking before
the rest of its declarations are dropped, 1 to 64. Without the bound
one file whose declarations all rank well fills `candidates` on its
own, and no other file reaches the candidate list however well it
would have ranked.

disabled.description:
Whether semantic ranking is off. Set it when the workspace must not
fetch model weights: search then answers lexically alone and raises no
preparation warning.

download_attempts.description:
Attempts one model download makes before semantic ranking degrades to
lexical for the life of the server, 1 to 10.

download_timeout.description: Wall-clock budget one model download has, 10s to 1h.

max_tokens.description:
Tokens the encoder reads from one declaration, 32 to 512. What follows
them is truncated.

max_vectors.description:
Vectors the workspace may hold, 1000 to 1000000. Embedding stops at the
bound and the search warning says so; each vector costs the model's
dimension in single-precision floats.

model.description:
Which weights: under `hf` a repository identifier such as
`minishlab/potion-retrieval-32M`, optionally carrying a revision after
`@`; under `directory` a workspace-relative directory holding them.
Vectors are stored per model, so changing the value embeds the
workspace again.

The model's own `config.json` decides how it is read. A `model_type` of
`model2vec` is a static model, which embeds a declaration by averaging
one row per token; anything else is read as a BERT checkpoint, which
runs a forward pass per batch and costs minutes rather than seconds
over a whole workspace.

source.description: Where the weights come from, which decides how `model` reads.

weight.description:
The semantic ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0. It and
`[search.lexical].weight` must sum to 1.

SemanticSource.description: Where the semantic ranking's model weights come from.

oneOf.description:
Weights come from a Hugging Face repository, cached where every
other Hugging Face client on the machine caches them.

Weights are a directory the workspace already holds. Nothing is
downloaded.

allOf.description: server.port and server.port_range are mutually exclusive

ServerConfiguration.description:
The `[server]` table. Filesystem scans and parses run on a bounded
worker pool; this table sets the worker count, bounds the queue wait,
sets how long the server serves with no request before it stops, and
selects the loopback port. The server reads the table at startup, so a
change applies on the next start.

idle_timeout.description: Wall-clock span with no served request that stops the server, 1s to 1d.

num_workers.description: Workers running blocking filesystem and parser operations at once, 1 to 64.

port.description:
The exact loopback port the server binds, 1024 or above. Excludes
`port_range`; omitted, the server picks from `port_range` or the
default serving range.

port_range.description:
The loopback range the server picks its port from. Excludes `port`;
omitted, the default serving range applies.

readiness_timeout.description:
Wall-clock bound one request waits for the workspace's index and
its language engines to prove they are ready to answer, 1s to 1h.
One deadline: index validation starts it, and once a request
resolves the languages it needs, waiting on those engines spends
what remains of it.

worker_queue_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound one request waits for a free worker, 1ms to 1h.

SourceConfiguration.description:
The `[source]` table: which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider
visible. `.git`, `.rift`, and `target` stay invisible whatever this table says.

exclude.description:
Exact file paths or globs dropped from visibility, in [`PathPattern`] syntax. A match
here is dropped even when `include` also matches it.

include.description:
Exact file paths or globs a file must match to stay visible, in [`PathPattern`] syntax.
Empty includes every file `exclude` and `.gitignore` leave standing.

respect_gitignore.description:
Whether the workspace's own `.gitignore` files, root and nested, hide the paths they
match. Global and parent-directory gitignore sources are never read.

TextSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.text]` table. `max_chunk` bounds lexical units derived from
visible text files.

max_chunk.description:
Bytes one lexical chunk may hold, 1kb to 16mb. Larger files are indexed as
several chunks of at most this size.

description:
The whole `rift.toml`. Every table is optional and defaults to the
behavior documented on it; any key outside these definitions refuses the
file as `configuration_invalid`.

engines.description:
Language engines keyed by name: each `[engines.<name>]` table names
an external LSP server and the languages it serves.

execution.description: Enablement and limits for caller-provided code.

hooks.description:
Hooks run in the changed tree, in list order, each time a change
applies.

logs.description:
The server's own log records: how many the workspace database keeps,
how many one read returns, and which targets are captured.

providers.description: Bounds and switches for the built-in providers.

search.description: Search ranking, visible text chunking, and storage bounds.

server.description: The server's own blocking-work bounds: worker count and queue wait.

source.description: Which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider visible.
